title: NANPA authority for shard-A NPAs 717, 720, 726 and 729

data.notes: Current NANPA materials identify 717 (Pennsylvania), 720 (Colorado), 726 (Texas) and 729 (Tennessee 423 overlay) as U.S. geographic NPAs. Each satisfies shard-A rule integer(NPA) mod 3 == 0; NANPA states 729 numbers became assignable beginning March 5, 2025.

title: Food Not Bombs Harrisburg current-status corroboration

data.notes: May 2026 Harrisburg public discussion reports Food Not Bombs Harrisburg serving a hot meal at Second and Market every Monday at 6 PM; a current Derry Township public biography independently states ongoing Monday meal volunteering with Food Not Bombs Harrisburg. Historical Food Not Bombs directory material is used only as a seed.

August 2026 public event listing identifies Harrisburg Free Store as a mutual-aid/free-store project at Broad Street Market with no money, barter or trade, and links its public event/Facebook surface; March and April 2026 listings corroborate recurring activity.

title: Denver Food Not Bombs current/recent public activity

data.notes: Current-accessible Denver DIY listing describes weekly Sunday Food Not Bombs Denver free-food distributions at 2180 Stout St and links the public Instagram @denverfoodnotbombs; a current Front Range mutual-aid resource hub also lists the same public account.

title: Little Read Books current first-party site

data.notes: Current 2026 first-party site describes Little Read Books as a Denver revolutionary socialist political-education collective with no owners, bosses or profit motive, operating a free bookstore and linking Instagram, Open Collective and Bookshop surfaces. Its Open Collective tags include anarchism, infoshop, mutual aid, free food and free shop.

title: Bread and Blankets Mutual Aid current first-party site

data.notes: Current first-party San Antonio site explicitly describes direct mutual aid to houseless neighbors, current February/summer 2026 supply work, public donation/contact surfaces and a goal of confronting systemic injustice and inequity; the City of San Antonio currently lists Bread and Blankets as a food-access partner.

title: Mootual Aid San Antonio current first-party site

data.notes: Current first-party site describes Mootual Aid as a flat autonomous San Antonio grassroots collective based on direct action, cooperation, solidarity and harm reduction, with public email and organizational phone surfaces.

title: Chattanooga DSA current first-party mutual-aid work

data.notes: Current first-party chapter site describes a Mutual Aid working group focused on food sovereignty, solidarity with unhoused neighbors, recurring community cooks and meal distributions, community fridges and political education; current join page exposes public email and communication signup.

title: Chattanooga Trans Liberation Collective current 2026 activity

data.publisher: Stove Works / Chattanooga Pride Food Coalition
data.notes: March 2026 Chattanooga event page names Chattanooga Trans Liberation Collective as an organizing partner; Chattanooga Pride's current Food Coalition page also lists the collective among organizers in a network coordinating free fridges, meal distribution and mutual aid.

title: Chattanooga Pride Food Coalition current first-party page

data.notes: Current first-party coalition page describes a partnership of local LGBTQ+ and allied organizations coordinating free fridges, meals, mutual aid and networks of care; organizers listed include Chattanooga Queer Empowerment Collective, Chattanooga Trans Liberation Collective and Mutual Aid Resource Library.
